newsitem.title: USA: US Airways pilots disappointed by "threat".
newsitem.headline: US Airways pilots disappointed by "threat".

text.p: US Airways Group Inc's pilots said Wednesday they were disappointed by the company's "threat" to downsize if it did not cut costs.

"It is unfortunate that the company chose to publicly threaten the employees," said Jim Gardner, a spokesman for the pilots union. "Both the pilots and management agree that long-term success is through growth," not downsizing, he said.
Earlier on Wednesday, US Airways said it experienced significant losses in key markets due to its "uncompetitive cost structure" and increasing competition from low-cost rivals.

The airline also said discussions to reduce costs "have now gone on for many years without progress." This lack of progress "leaves us no choice but to conclude that the company must promptly implement the appropriate steps to address the issue," the company said.
If the company did not get a competitive cost structure in place, it said it might be forced to become a smaller, regional carrier.

The pilots' union disputed US Airways' assertion that no progress has been made in contract talks. The pilots said strides have been made, but progress has been slow. The two sides continued contract talks Wednesday in Washington.

The union also said it has been in talks with the airline about plans to create a low-cost unit to compete with low-cost carriers such as Southwest Airlines Co and Delta Air Lines Inc's Express unit. The two sides disagree on the size the low-cost unit should be.
Although the pilots disputed some of the airline's comments, the union applauded the company's strong first quarter results.

US Airways posted first quarter earnings of $1.45 per fully diluted share on revenues of $2.1 billion, topping the consensus analysts' estimate of $0.69 a share, according to First Call. For the first quarter last year, US Airways posted a loss of $0.86 per fully diluted share on revenues of $1.9 billion.
